  "explanation": "With Q = {p : p | A} the two flagged claims are indeed false (e.g. A=15, x=21: P(x)={3,7} all \u2264 A but \u03c3(x)={3}; and 7 \u2208 P(x)\\\u03c3(x) is < A), so the objection's local claim is correct. However every other use in the text reads Q as the primes \u2264 A: 'necessarily a prime at most A', 'Every prime in \u03c3(b) is at most A, whereas every prime in P(x)\\\u03c3(x) is greater than A', and the falsification section states 'This forced the larger, but still finite, set of all primes at most A.' With that reading the erasure argument (R\u00b7q | x so Rp^k < Rq \u2264 x; skipped m yields a coprime earlier term b, contradiction) is complete for all terms. So a misprinted definition plus its false one-line rationale stands beside a valid argument; fixing 'p | A' to 'p \u2264 A' and deleting that rationale repairs it."
